sentences.text: This crocodilian had a skull measuring approximately 20 centimeters in length and reached a total estimated length of around 1.6 meters.
Its jaws featured sharp, recurved teeth with narrow bases, while its back was covered in rectangular osteoderms with a medial crest running along the dorsal surface.
The species name D. piscator was chosen based on the inference that the animal could catch fish, deduced from the specific shape of its teeth.
Although it may have eaten turtles, the animal was better adapted to prey on smaller animals like fish.
The genus Duerosuchus was named after the Duero River because its fossils were found in the Duero River Basin in Corrales del Vino, Spain.

A 2021 phylogenetic study placed Duerosuchus in the family Planocraniidae, resolving earlier uncertainty about its classification as a basal crocodilian closely related to short-snouted forms like alligatoroids.
Duerosuchus lived during the Lutetian stage, between 48.07 and 41.03 million years ago.
The lack of Duerosuchus fossils in other Eocene deposits on the Iberian Peninsula makes it difficult to determine its chronological and stratigraphic distribution.
